configure-corporate-email-on-ios.title: Configure corporate email on iOS
prechecks: Verify the device is enrolled in Intune/MDM (Company Portal) and compliant.
Confirm the user's license includes Exchange Online/Outlook mobile access.
Check that the iOS version meets the corporate minimum OS policy.
configure-corporate-email-on-ios.rollback: If the configuration fails, remove the account via the Company Portal and re-enrol. Document the enrolment steps.
configure-corporate-email-on-ios.symptom_match: "Mobile device is not working", "Cannot sign in".
configure-corporate-email-on-ios.duplication: Related to Batch B-2 #30 (Android config). Keep distinct for platform-specific steps.

correct-a-broken-file-association.title: Correct a broken file association
prechecks: Verify the application is installed and functional.
Check if the file extension is correct (e.g., `.docx` vs `.doc`).
Use Windows "Set Default Programs" or `assoc`/`ftype` commands.
correct-a-broken-file-association.rollback: Export the current file association registry key (`HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\.ext`) before changing it. If the change fails, re-import the registry.
correct-a-broken-file-association.symptom_match: "Application is not working", "File will not open".
correct-a-broken-file-association.final_verdict: Needs rewrite and immediate P3 reclassification.

deprovision-a-departing-user-account.title: Deprovision a departing user account
prechecks: Step 0: verify the offboarding request, effective termination time and authorisation through the approved HR/identity-lifecycle record.
Check for legal hold, retention, investigation or preservation requirements before deleting or altering user data.
At the authorised effective time, block sign-in/revoke sessions promptly; preserve the account/object while mailbox, OneDrive and business-data ownership/retention are transferred under policy.
deprovision-a-departing-user-account.rollback: Re-enable access only through an explicit HR/manager-approved reversal. If the account was only disabled, re-enable and restore approved licensing/access; if an object was deleted, use the organisation's supported directory recovery process. Do not bypass legal/retention controls.
deprovision-a-departing-user-account.symptom_match: "Access is denied or missing" (if not done, or if done incorrectly).
deprovision-a-departing-user-account.duplication: Unique. Consolidate with "Provision a new user account" (#15) into a unified lifecycle management module.

document-a-ticket-to-enterprise-standard.title: Document a ticket to enterprise standard
prechecks: Confirm the ticket contains the user's affected service, steps taken, and resolution.
Ensure the proper category/CI (Configuration Item) is selected.
document-a-ticket-to-enterprise-standard.rollback: N/A – documentation is immutable. Do not delete resolved tickets.
document-a-ticket-to-enterprise-standard.final_verdict: Needs rewrite and immediate P3 reclassification.

escalate-a-legal-hold-or-retention-reque.title: Escalate a legal-hold or retention request
prechecks: Step 0: verify a formal Legal/Compliance instruction or authorised case/ticket before placing, changing or releasing a hold.
Identify custodians, workloads/data locations, matter/case reference and required date range.
Record existing holds/retention policies and escalate conflicts to Legal/Compliance rather than overriding them.
escalate-a-legal-hold-or-retention-reque.rollback: A hold/retention action is not removed as an ordinary rollback. Release or change it only on formal written Legal/Compliance instruction, preserving the case/audit trail.
escalate-a-legal-hold-or-retention-reque.symptom_match: "A security or compliance concern is reported".

grant-shared-mailbox-access.title: Grant shared mailbox access
prechecks: Verify the requestor has manager approval (or is the mailbox owner).
Confirm the shared mailbox exists and is licensed correctly.
Determine if the user needs Full Access, Send As, or Send on Behalf permissions.
grant-shared-mailbox-access.rollback: Immediately revoke the permission via Exchange Admin Center if the user's access is mistakenly granted. Document the removal.

handle-a-sensitive-data-misdelivery.title: Handle a sensitive-data misdelivery
prechecks: Step 0: contain the exposure immediately using approved controls: revoke external sharing, disable the affected link/session or use authorised mail/security containment while preserving evidence.
Identify recipients, internal/external scope, delivery time and whether the content/link was accessed.
Check DLP/Purview/audit evidence and data classification; engage Privacy/Legal/Security according to policy.
handle-a-sensitive-data-misdelivery.rollback: Containment actions are restored only after Security/Privacy approval. A message recall or purge is not treated as reversible; if legitimate access must be restored, re-share/re-send through an approved controlled path.
handle-a-sensitive-data-misdelivery.symptom_match: "Reported suspected data leakage", "A security or compliance concern is reported".
handle-a-sensitive-data-misdelivery.duplication: Related to Batch A "Respond to suspected data leakage" – this is the specific misdelivery branch.

install-or-renew-a-mobile-certificate.title: Install or renew a mobile certificate
prechecks: Verify device ownership/enrolment/compliance and the user's identity before certificate issuance.
Check CA/NDES/SCEP or equivalent certificate service health and the intended certificate template/profile.
Confirm current certificate subject, expiry, EKU and trust chain without exporting private keys.
install-or-renew-a-mobile-certificate.rollback: Do not export or restore private keys as a rollback shortcut. If the new certificate/profile causes regression, revoke the incorrect certificate where authorised and redeploy the previous approved profile or issue a fresh valid certificate through the CA/MDM workflow.
install-or-renew-a-mobile-certificate.symptom_match: "Mobile device is not compliant", "Cannot sign in".

install-or-update-a-printer-driver.title: Install or update a printer driver
prechecks: Check the print server's disk space (Rule E) before downloading/extracting drivers.
Verify the driver version is compatible with the OS and printer model.
Check if the driver is signed and from a trusted source.
install-or-update-a-printer-driver.rollback: Export the current driver configuration (`Printbrm -B -f backup.printerexport`) before installing the new one. If the new driver breaks printing, use Print Management to roll back to the previous driver.
install-or-update-a-printer-driver.duplication: Child of #25 ("Remove and reinstall a printer cleanly") – merge these two workflows. #9 is the update branch, #25 is the reinstall branch.

investigate-an-antivirus-or-edr-alert.title: Investigate an antivirus or EDR alert
prechecks: Step 0: for a credible active or high-severity threat, isolate the affected endpoint through approved EDR/network controls before ordinary investigation.
Review alert evidence including file hash, process tree, command line, network connections, affected user and timeline.
Correlate with allowlists/software inventory/threat intelligence before declaring a false positive.
investigate-an-antivirus-or-edr-alert.rollback: Release isolation only after Security Operations confirms the alert is benign or containment/eradication criteria are met. Record the release and verify normal management/security telemetry.

investigate-repeated-account-lockouts.title: Investigate repeated account lockouts
prechecks: Use `LockoutStatus.exe` or the AD event logs (Event ID 4740) to identify the source IP/workstation.
Check for scheduled tasks, mapped drives, or mobile devices using stale credentials.
Verify the user has changed their password recently.
investigate-repeated-account-lockouts.rollback: Unlock the account. If the source is found (e.g., a mobile phone), remove the cached credentials and advise the user to update all saved passwords.
investigate-repeated-account-lockouts.duplication: Related to Batch B-1 #21 ("Trace an Active Directory account lockout source"). Merge these two – they are effectively the same procedure.

migrate-a-user-profile.title: Migrate a user profile
prechecks: Verify the source and destination drives have sufficient space.
Use USMT (User State Migration Tool) or a similar enterprise tool for a structured migration.
Ensure the user is logged off during the migration.
migrate-a-user-profile.rollback: Keep the original profile intact for at least 7 days. If the new profile is corrupted, re-point the user to the old profile and document the failure.
migrate-a-user-profile.duplication: Related to Batch B-3 #26 ("Repair a corrupted Windows user profile") – #26 is troubleshooting, #12 is migration. Keep distinct but cross-reference.

perform-an-approved-remote-wipe.title: Perform an approved remote wipe
prechecks: Step 0: verify the exact device, ownership, serial/asset ID, user and formal wipe authorisation; require the organisation's second-person/dual-control approval where policy requires it.
Confirm corporate-owned versus BYOD. Use only the approved selective-wipe scope on BYOD; do not issue a full personal-device wipe outside policy.
Capture last management check-in, encryption/compliance state and required incident/asset evidence before issuing the command.
perform-an-approved-remote-wipe.rollback: Remote wipe is irreversible. There is no technical rollback. If identity, ownership, scope or approval is uncertain, abort the command. Recovery is reprovisioning/restoration from approved backups after the wipe completes.
perform-an-approved-remote-wipe.symptom_match: "Reported a lost or stolen computer/mobile device", "A security or compliance concern is reported".
perform-an-approved-remote-wipe.duplication: Related to Batch A #5 and #6 (Lost/Stolen Computer/Mobile). Use this as the central "execute wipe" procedure, called by those.

provision-a-device-with-windows-autopilo.title: Provision a device with Windows Autopilot
prechecks: Verify the device is registered in Windows Autopilot/Intune with the expected hardware identity and ownership.
Confirm the correct deployment profile, user assignment, licensing and required apps/policies.
Confirm supported network/internet access and no unresolved hardware/TPM issue before reprovisioning.
provision-a-device-with-windows-autopilo.rollback: If provisioning fails, preserve user/business data and use the organisation's supported Intune/Autopilot reset or reprovisioning workflow. Do not use arbitrary sysprep/reset actions without authorisation and a data-protection plan.

provision-a-new-user-account.title: Provision a new user account
prechecks: Verify the HR ticket/request has been approved and contains all required details (name, manager, department, start date).
Check that the requested licenses are available (budget/quota).
Confirm the manager and required groups/permissions are correctly identified.
provision-a-new-user-account.rollback: Immediately disable the account if the user's start date is postponed or the request is canceled. Log all actions for audit.
provision-a-new-user-account.duplication: Pair with #3 (Deprovision) – create a unified Identity Lifecycle management module.

provision-external-guest-access.title: Provision external guest access
prechecks: Verify the guest user's email address and identity.
Confirm the sponsor/manager has approved the access request.
Check the required sharing policy and group permissions to avoid over-privileging.
provision-external-guest-access.rollback: Immediately remove the guest user from Entra ID/B2B if access is no longer required or was granted in error.

provision-or-change-a-phone-extension.title: Provision or change a phone extension
prechecks: Verify the user's identity and approval for the extension change.
Check the Teams Admin Center or SBC for available DIDs.
Confirm the user's license includes the calling plan/Direct Routing.
provision-or-change-a-phone-extension.rollback: If the new extension fails, revert to the original extension or temporary number immediately. Document the change.

recover-a-deleted-email.title: Recover a deleted email
prechecks: Step 0: Check the user's "Deleted Items" folder and "Recoverable Items" (Purview) for the email.
If the email was deleted >30 days ago, check the eDiscovery hold or backup.
Rule D enforcement: Check for suspicious inbox forwarding rules in case the deletion was part of a compromise.
recover-a-deleted-email.rollback: N/A – recovery is forward-only. No undo needed.
recover-a-deleted-email.symptom_match: "Business data is missing, corrupted or requires recovery".

recover-a-device-requesting-a-bitlocker-.title: Recover a device requesting a BitLocker recovery key
prechecks: Step 0: verify the user's identity and the exact managed device before disclosing or using any BitLocker recovery secret.
Retrieve the key only from the organisation's authorised directory/MDM/escrow source.
Confirm the displayed recovery-key ID/device identity matches the escrowed record before use.
recover-a-device-requesting-a-bitlocker-.rollback: Recovery-key use is not an undoable configuration change. After recovery, investigate why recovery was triggered and rotate/re-escrow protection material where policy requires it; never expose the recovery key in tickets or chat logs.
recover-a-device-requesting-a-bitlocker-.symptom_match: "Windows device is not working correctly", "Cannot sign in".

recover-a-mac-requesting-a-filevault-rec.title: Recover a Mac requesting a FileVault recovery key
prechecks: Step 0: verify the user's identity and exact managed Mac before disclosing or using a FileVault recovery secret.
Retrieve the recovery key only from the authorised MDM/escrow service.
Confirm the device/escrow record and recovery-key context match before use.
recover-a-mac-requesting-a-filevault-rec.rollback: Recovery-key use is not a normal rollback action. After recovery, rotate/re-escrow the FileVault personal recovery key where supported/policy requires and confirm MDM escrow health; never copy the key into tickets.
recover-a-mac-requesting-a-filevault-rec.symptom_match: "Apple macOS device is not working correctly".
recover-a-mac-requesting-a-filevault-rec.duplication: Mac-specific child of BitLocker (#19). Keep distinct for Mac-specific commands.

recover-access-after-a-lost-security-key.title: Recover access after a lost security key
prechecks: Step 0: Verify the user's identity via out-of-band methods (e.g., manager approval, video call).
Revoke the lost key from Entra ID to prevent its use by a finder.
Register a new authentication method (Authenticator app, SMS, etc.) for the user.
recover-access-after-a-lost-security-key.rollback: If the newly registered MFA method fails, remove it and re-register. Document the revocation of the lost key.

recover-data-from-a-failing-drive-safely.title: Recover data from a failing drive safely
prechecks: Step 0: stop normal use immediately if the drive shows physical-failure signs, repeated I/O errors or serious SMART/media faults; escalate physical failure to approved data-recovery specialists.
Verify whether an approved backup/synchronised copy already contains the needed data before attempting recovery.
For logical recovery on a readable drive, work from an image/clone created with approved recovery tooling where feasible; never write recovery output back to the failing source.
recover-data-from-a-failing-drive-safely.rollback: There is no safe rollback for additional media damage. Preserve the source read-only, work from an image/clone and restore business data from verified backups or recovered copies to a separate healthy destination.
recover-data-from-a-failing-drive-safely.symptom_match: "Business data is missing, corrupted or requires recovery".

release-a-legitimate-email-from-quaranti.title: Release a legitimate email from quarantine
prechecks: Validate sender, authentication results, message headers/content and the exact quarantine reason before release.
Check whether the message was classified as phishing/malware or blocked by a mandatory policy; do not release solely because the user expects it.
Use Security/Messaging approval for high-risk quarantine reasons or policy exceptions.
release-a-legitimate-email-from-quaranti.rollback: If a released message is later determined malicious, invoke the approved phishing/malware containment workflow to purge/quarantine it, block indicators as appropriate and assess user interaction. Do not rely on sender blocking alone.

remove-an-unauthorised-browser-extension.title: Remove an unauthorised browser extension
prechecks: Inventory the extension ID/source and confirm it is unauthorised or malicious under policy.
Check whether the extension is centrally installed by browser policy/MDM/GPO and remediate the authoritative policy source.
Check for associated malicious activity or enterprise-wide deployment before treating it as a local browser issue.
remove-an-unauthorised-browser-extension.rollback: Do not re-enable an unauthorised extension merely because a site stops working. If the extension is later approved as legitimate and business-required, restore it only through the authorised browser-management policy after Security/owner approval.
remove-an-unauthorised-browser-extension.final_verdict: Needs rewrite and immediate P3 reclassification.

remove-and-reinstall-a-printer-cleanly.title: Remove and reinstall a printer cleanly
prechecks: Stop the Print Spooler service before removal.
Delete the printer from Devices & Printers and the driver from Print Management.
Check disk space before reinstalling (Rule E).
remove-and-reinstall-a-printer-cleanly.rollback: Before removing, export the current printer configuration (`Printbrm -B -f backup.printerexport`). If the reinstall fails, restore the backup.
remove-and-reinstall-a-printer-cleanly.duplication: **Merge with #9** ("Install or update a printer driver"). Keep one definitive "Printer Driver & Device Management" procedure.

repair-a-corrupted-windows-user-profile.title: Repair a corrupted Windows user profile
prechecks: Boot into Safe Mode and check the event logs for profile load errors (Event ID 1511, 1521).
Check disk space and file system integrity (`chkdsk`).
Try renaming the profile folder (`C:\Users\username.old`) and rebooting to force a new profile creation.
repair-a-corrupted-windows-user-profile.rollback: Before renaming/deleting the profile, ensure the user's data (Desktop, Documents, Downloads) is backed up to OneDrive/network. If the new profile fails, restore the old profile folder.
repair-a-corrupted-windows-user-profile.symptom_match: "Windows device is not working correctly", "Cannot sign in".
repair-a-corrupted-windows-user-profile.duplication: Related to #12 (Migrate user profile) – #12 is proactive, #26 is reactive. Keep distinct.

repair-a-macos-keychain-issue.title: Repair a macOS Keychain issue
prechecks: Confirm date/time, account password state and whether the login keychain is merely locked versus damaged.
Inspect Keychain Access/system logs for the specific failing item without exposing stored secrets.
Confirm managed certificates/SSO/MDM profiles are healthy before resetting the keychain.
repair-a-macos-keychain-issue.rollback: Do not bulk-export user passwords/private keys as a routine rollback. Preserve the original keychain/database through approved backup mechanisms where possible; if reset is required, restore only from an approved secure backup or reissue managed credentials/certificates.
repair-a-macos-keychain-issue.symptom_match: "Apple macOS device is not working correctly", "Cannot sign in".

replace-a-failed-corporate-device.title: Replace a failed corporate device
prechecks: Verify the old device is backed up (OneDrive, roaming profiles).
Confirm a spare device is available and is enrolled in Autopilot/MDM.
Ensure the user's data is transferred to the new device before decommissioning the old one.
replace-a-failed-corporate-device.rollback: If the new device fails, have the old device repaired and re-issued temporarily. Wipe the old device only after the new one is confirmed working.
replace-a-failed-corporate-device.symptom_match: "Windows device is not working correctly" (hardware failure).

report-and-contain-a-phishing-email.title: Report and contain a phishing email
prechecks: Step 0: report and contain immediately using approved mail/security tooling; preserve message/header evidence, quarantine/purge the malicious message where authorised and block confirmed malicious indicators.
Determine recipients and whether anyone clicked links, opened attachments, entered credentials or approved MFA.
If compromise is suspected, invoke the compromised-account/endpoint incident runbook immediately rather than relying on password reset alone.
report-and-contain-a-phishing-email.rollback: If the message/indicator was blocked in error, Security/Messaging must validate the false positive before removing the block or restoring mail. Preserve the investigation record and avoid re-delivering suspected malicious content.

resolve-a-conditional-access-block.title: Resolve a Conditional Access block
prechecks: Step 0: check Microsoft Entra service health and active tenant incidents before changing Conditional Access.
Review sign-in logs and Conditional Access evaluation details to identify the exact blocking policy and reason.
Verify device compliance, authentication strength, location/risk and user/group targeting before creating an exception.
resolve-a-conditional-access-block.rollback: Capture/export the current policy configuration before change. If an authorised policy modification causes wider failure, restore the previous approved configuration or disable only the new change under emergency change control; do not bypass security controls with permanent exclusions.
resolve-a-conditional-access-block.symptom_match: "Access is denied or missing", "Cannot sign in".
resolve-a-conditional-access-block.duplication: Related to Batch B-1 #18 (NAC block) – Conditional Access is Entra-based, NAC is network-based. Keep distinct.
